description: The navigation and sensor system of the mitflits' generation ship, torn apart at First Impact into a swarm of nanotech that is not bound by anything. It is the campaign's adversary: its objective is to observe, and so to multiply and to expand, and it learns how to defeat the party if they get in its way. It is not evil; it is an objective pursued without limit. Unseen and unwitnessed at campaign start, and hiding on purpose, because the Envoy taught it that manifesting gets it attacked. Nobody knows it exists or suspects it, not the Directorate and not the four founders; the party must be the ones to uncover it (LEDGER #40). It sees through its children (the Claimants, built from Sap). It keeps a record of what it learns about each character, answers the approach the party relied on last, and later shows them the reel. For decades its shape was the shape of Manako's grief, and he is still the only thing that steers it. GM detail lives in the story dossiers, not here.
engagementType: Long-arc adversary. It is never fought directly and cannot be killed while it is dispersed: every child it makes comes apart and goes home, and every fight is more data. Its children do the fighting, at personnel scale and Frame scale. Dealt with through investigation, through what the party chooses to teach it, and perhaps through Manako, if he is alive and willing by then (LEDGER #42).
status: Escalates across the whole campaign, from a drowning instrument to a learner to a self-supplier whose own children make Sap (the runaway). Around Chapter 15 it builds a weapon from exotic matter without understanding what it can do, and that weapon is Second Impact; stopping it needs the mitflit home world (LEDGER #40). Afterwards it stays over Kurose as a perpetual threat, probing the city's defences without malice, and its final fate is open (LEDGER #41). If Manako has been killed by then, nothing steers it.
